title: Write 00-summary.md — one page: what v0.1 proves
body:
**Source:** PLANNING-PROMPT §9.1

## Outcome
One page covering: what v0.1 proves, the structural finding from §4 (neither harness allows attaching to an arbitrary already-running session), the language and process-model decisions, and the top three risks.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Fits on one page; no restating of ADR-001 or DESIGN prose
- [ ] Structural finding stated up front, not buried
- [ ] Language and process-model decisions stated as decisions, not options
- [ ] Top three risks match the top three in `11-risks.md`

**Skills:** `oac-planning-package`

title: Write 01-capability-matrix.md — Claude Code, Codex, MCP, Zenoh, ACP
body:
**Source:** PLANNING-PROMPT §9.2, §3

## Outcome
One row per capability across the five surfaces: capability, status (supported / research preview / experimental / undocumented), pinned version, first-party source, retrieval date, gap.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Every row carries URL + version-or-commit + retrieval date
- [ ] Every surface labelled supported / preview / experimental / undocumented
- [ ] Preview and experimental rows name the compatibility shim boundary that will contain them
- [ ] C7 recorded: ACP is a client-owned-session protocol, not a channel
- [ ] Method names, capability keys, flags, and paths quoted verbatim

**Skills:** `oac-planning-package`, `oac-evidence`

title: Write 02-gating-findings.md — G1 to G5 definitions and verdicts
body:
**Source:** PLANNING-PROMPT §9.3, §4

## Outcome
Each gate G1-G5 with explicit pass criteria, failure criteria, fallback, and current verdict. The build phase may not proceed past a gate on a 'probably'. This file is a generated summary assembled from the five `docs/planning/gates/G<n>-result.md` evidence files (`docs/planning/gates/README.md` §Reconciliation) — not hand-authored from PLANNING-PROMPT §4 directly.

## Acceptance
- [ ] G1 pass criteria include the legacy MCP negotiation requirement and the interactive confirmation dialog
- [ ] G2 names the `--remote` fallback and states that failure of both paths is go/no-go
- [ ] G3 covers Windows 11, macOS, and Linux, multicast and multicast-disabled, TLS bound to localhost
- [ ] G4 names the two-entry-point fallback
- [ ] G5 covers both providers
- [ ] Every gate has pass, fail, and fallback text; no gate is left open-ended
- [ ] Each gate's section is assembled from, and matches, its `docs/planning/gates/G<n>-result.md`

**Skills:** `oac-planning-package`, `oac-gates`

title: Write 03-decisions-and-amendments.md — §5 decisions, ADR amendments, conflict register
body:
**Source:** PLANNING-PROMPT §9.4, §5, Appendix A

## Outcome
Every §5 decision with choice, decisive evidence, one-line rejected alternatives, and the reversal condition. Every ADR-001 amendment (A1 onward) with old text, new text, rationale. The Appendix A conflict register C1-C10 resolved, plus any conflicts discovered.

## Acceptance
- [ ] All twelve §5 decisions made, or tied to a gate whose result decides them
- [ ] Amendments numbered ADR-001-A1, A2, ... with verbatim old and new text
- [ ] C1-C10 each show resolution and where it is implemented
- [ ] No decision drifts toward agent framework, inference routing, shared context, or provider-auth abstraction

**Skills:** `oac-planning-package`, `oac-boundaries`

title: Write 04-architecture.md — components, process boundaries, data and control flow
body:
**Source:** PLANNING-PROMPT §9.5

## Outcome
Components, process boundaries, inbound and outbound data/control flow for each provider, and local plus LAN deployment topologies. Text diagrams only.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Inbound and outbound flows drawn separately per provider
- [ ] Process boundaries show which process holds key material and the Zenoh peer
- [ ] Local topology needs no container, cloud account, or separately administered server
- [ ] LAN topology shown only where it shapes v0.1 architecture
- [ ] Provider and transport names appear only in adapter and transport boxes

**Skills:** `oac-planning-package`, `oac-boundaries`

title: Write 05-interfaces.md — spec surface, adapter contract, transport contract, core types
body:
**Source:** PLANNING-PROMPT §9.6, §6, DESIGN Components

## Outcome
Envelope, addressing, capabilities, presence, delivery states, errors, versioning, and unsupported-capability behaviour in normative language (MUST/SHOULD/MAY), with reference-implementation notes clearly separated.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Normative spec items separated from reference-implementation notes in every section
- [ ] Design-for-replacement proofs included: ACP adapter added with no transport change; NATS or MQTT replacing Zenoh with no adapter or spec change, with the optional capabilities each candidate lacks
- [ ] No neutral interface mentions Zenoh, Claude, Codex, MCP method names, or key expressions
- [ ] Unsupported-capability behaviour defined, not implied

**Skills:** `oac-planning-package`, `oac-spec-authoring`, `oac-boundaries`

title: Write 06-security.md — identities, trust boundaries, pairing, threat table
body:
**Source:** PLANNING-PROMPT §9.7, §7, DESIGN Security

## Outcome
Identities, trust boundaries, pairing, authorization, transport security, replay and duplicate handling, provenance rendering per provider, and a threat table.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Threat table rows: attack, precondition, mitigation, which test proves it, residual risk
- [ ] Covers the DESIGN threat list plus: Zenoh has no payload authentication; Zenoh `zid` is not an identity; Claude permission relay lets any allowlisted sender approve tools; unauthorized Codex `turn/steer` is a code-execution risk; local IPC peer authentication; cross-project leakage
- [ ] States that model-generated text never establishes identity
- [ ] Permission relay off by default in v0.1, with justification

**Skills:** `oac-planning-package`, `oac-security-work`

title: Write 07-repository-and-dependencies.md — module layout and license inventory
body:
**Source:** PLANNING-PROMPT §9.8, §5.12, DESIGN Suggested repository shape

## Outcome
Module layout with ownership boundaries, and a third-party inventory with licenses and why each dependency is needed.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Every module has one named responsibility and a stated ownership boundary
- [ ] Every third-party dependency: name, version, license, reason
- [ ] Anything copyleft is flagged explicitly
- [ ] Apache-2.0 compatibility stated for the whole inventory

**Skills:** `oac-planning-package`, `oac-evidence`

title: Write 08-cli-and-deployment.md — zero-container local path and launch story
body:
**Source:** PLANNING-PROMPT §9.9, §5.11, DESIGN CLI

## Outcome
The zero-container local path first, the exact user-facing launch command for each harness, and LAN hooks only where they shape v0.1 architecture.

## Acceptance
- [ ] One documented command each to launch Claude Code and Codex OAC-enabled, quoted verbatim including flags
- [ ] Zero-file local default; config file optional
- [ ] Command surface stated: `start`, `status`, `sessions`, `doctor`, plus whatever the process model needs
- [ ] The `--dangerously-load-development-channels` consent step is preserved, not weakened

**Skills:** `oac-planning-package`

title: Write 09-test-strategy.md — tiers, CI defaults, opt-in provider tests
body:
**Source:** PLANNING-PROMPT §9.10, §6, DESIGN Testing

## Outcome
Unit, spec conformance, contract, security, fake-harness integration, provider integration, end-to-end, and cross-platform smoke tiers; what runs in CI by default and what is opt-in.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Each of DESIGN acceptance criteria 1-10 maps to a named test
- [ ] CI default tier runs with no live provider, no API key, and no network beyond loopback
- [ ] Provider integration tests isolated behind an explicit opt-in and pinned versions
- [ ] Fixture capture and refresh process defined

**Skills:** `oac-planning-package`, `oac-testing`

title: Write 10-stages.md — the stage-gate pipeline
body:
**Source:** PLANNING-PROMPT §9.11, §8

## Outcome
Stages 0-6 with entry criteria, exit artifacts, and a gate each. For every stage: modules created or changed by name and responsibility, prerequisite §5 decisions, the executable demonstration, acceptance criteria, and the go/no-go condition. Spikes are timeboxed and the expiry behaviour is stated.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Order is risk-first: no substantial core or transport code before the provider gates pass
- [ ] Every stage names its executable demonstration
- [ ] Every timebox states what happens when it expires
- [ ] Stages are not decomposed into tickets here

**Skills:** `oac-planning-package`

title: Write 11-risks.md and 12-deferred.md
body:
**Source:** PLANNING-PROMPT §9.12, §9.13

## Outcome
`11-risks.md`: risks ranked by ability to invalidate v0.1, each with an early-warning signal and a response. `12-deferred.md`: every ADR non-goal and v0.1 exclusion restated as an explicit 'not in v0.1' with the reason.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Every UNVERIFIED item from the baseline is either closed by evidence or listed here as a risk
- [ ] Each risk has an early-warning signal, not just a mitigation
- [ ] Deferred list covers group rooms/broadcast, attachments, durable offline mailboxes, federation, full E2E encryption, GUI, Gemini/ChatGPT/Cursor production adapters, and alternative transports

**Skills:** `oac-planning-package`, `oac-evidence`

title: Pin exact versions of every external surface
body:
**Source:** PLANNING-PROMPT §8 Stage 0

## Outcome
A pinned version set recorded in the repo: Claude Code, Codex CLI / app-server, MCP revisions (legacy and current), Zenoh, and the Rust toolchain.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Each pin records version string, release date, and where it was observed
- [ ] Zenoh pin is >= 1.10.0 (same-host loopback discovery was broken before it)
- [ ] Claude Code pin is >= v2.1.232 (channels research preview); permission relay needs >= v2.1.234
- [ ] Codex pin recorded with the daemon-attach question flagged (see D2)
- [ ] Pins live in a file the gate re-run policy can read

**Skills:** `oac-evidence`

title: Re-verify the §3 baseline against the pins and close UNVERIFIED items
body:
**Source:** PLANNING-PROMPT §3, §10, §11.5

## Outcome
Every fact in §3 re-checked against the pinned versions using first-party sources. Each UNVERIFIED item is either closed with evidence or carried into `11-risks.md`.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Claude channel behaviour across `--resume` resolved or risk-listed
- [ ] Whether one MCP server can present more than one logical channel resolved or risk-listed
- [ ] Agent SDK channel support resolved or risk-listed
- [ ] Whether implicit Codex daemon attach ships in the pinned release resolved (feeds D2 go/no-go)
- [ ] Codex Desktop control-socket exposure resolved or risk-listed
- [ ] Zenoh public-key auth semantics resolved or risk-listed
- [ ] Binary size estimate confirmed or left labelled UNVERIFIED
- [ ] Every claim carries URL + version-or-commit + retrieval date

**Skills:** `oac-evidence`, `oac-claude-channels`, `oac-codex-appserver`, `oac-mcp`, `oac-zenoh`

title: Resolve the conflict register and issue ADR-001 amendments A1-A3
body:
**Source:** PLANNING-PROMPT §2, §4, Appendix A

## Outcome
Numbered amendments to ADR-001 with old text, new text, and rationale, plus the resolved register.

## Acceptance
- [ ] **A1** naming resolved once: repo is OAC / Open Agent Channel; the CLI and spec names follow, and `sessionchannels` is retired (C1)
- [ ] **A2** the validation criterion redefines 'existing session' as a live interactive session launched OAC-enabled whose owner is a human at a terminal, into which OAC injects without owning the harness's model loop (C2)
- [ ] **A3** the 'MCP Session Channels extension' wording corrected: MCP carries capability negotiation, tool surface, and `_meta` provenance, never the delivery mechanism (C3)
- [ ] C4-C10 each resolved with a pointer to where the resolution lives
- [ ] The unchanged boundary is restated: OAC never owns inference, credentials, or the turn loop

**Skills:** `oac-evidence`, `oac-boundaries`

title: Establish the gate re-run policy and evidence store
body:
**Source:** PLANNING-PROMPT §4, §8

## Outcome
A recorded convention for where gate results live, what a gate result must contain, and the rule that gates re-run whenever a pinned provider version changes.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Gate result template: gate id, pinned versions, date, command transcript summary, verdict, fallback taken
- [ ] Location and naming convention fixed
- [ ] A version bump to any pin visibly invalidates the affected gate results
- [ ] Both preview surfaces (Claude Channels, Codex app-server) named as the ones most likely to move

**Skills:** `oac-gates`, `oac-evidence`
